Subject: Dedicated commit — need a contingency plan for GPU market shock

Hannah / Karthik,

Thanks again for the detailed sizing call yesterday. Helios is comfortable with the overall committed capacity, but our CFO pushed back on the tail risk: if GPU spot/index prices spike materially in year 1–2, we want clarity on how Redwood will protect unit economics or compensate.

Two specific asks from finance:
- A simple stress table showing our committed SKU cost at +30%, +60%, +100% GPU price moves (same assumptions you used on the call).
- A proposal for a one-time protective credit or discount trigger so we aren't stuck paying deeply elevated unit rates without remedy.

We have an internal board meeting on July 7 where we need to present the mitigation and ask for approval on the commit. Can you get a short ops-level proposal and recommended approval path by end of day July 1?

Attaching our internal sensitivity assumptions (see helios-stress-scenarios.xlsx).

—Jonathan

Jonathan — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. We can definitely put a concise ops proposal together. High level plan I'm proposing internally (will send a one-page PDF and a short Ops deck):

1) Stress table (by SKU): match Helios assumptions and show delta to list price, expected pass-through, and net effective unit after our proposed protections.
2) Risk-sharing mechanism (recommended): a tiered temporary credit that kicks in when a published GPU market index (third-party) moves >X% vs baseline for a sustained 14-day window. Credit declines by tranche (e.g., 40% of incremental cost at +30%, 60% at +60%, capped at 6 months).
3) Approval path: Sales -> Finance (Marcus) -> Legal (Neha) -> Head of Revenue (exec signoff). Marcus — can you confirm if a credit of this structure is finance-OK as a one-off, and whether we should gate the term on total committed dollars? Neha — any legal red flags on a contingent credit tied to an external index?
4) Asks of Helios: agree to the index reference, approve the mutual action plan addendum, and sign the updated term sheet.

If we can lock internal approval by July 2, I can send an updated term sheet and a DocuSign link for Helios to execute on July 3 — that should hit your July 7 board window.

I'll attach the draft term language and a short stress-summary.

—Hannah

Hannah / team — reviewed. Quick finance view and concrete numbers below (assumptions: current GPU index baseline = $X/token-equivalent; committed volume profile per Helios MLP; we model three sensitivity bands):

- Scenario A (+30% GPU index): incremental cost to Redwood = $62k over 12 months; recommended temporary credit = 40% of incremental cost (one-time credit applied across first 3 monthly invoices).
- Scenario B (+60%): incremental cost = $145k; recommended credit = 50% of incremental cost (applied across 6 months).
- Scenario C (+100%): incremental cost = $320k; recommend fallback to a capped protection: either a tiered credit (60% of incremental cost) or option to convert a portion of reserved SKU to burstable credits with lower minimums — whichever is cleaner legally.

Finance constraints: we cannot extend an open-ended refund liability. Credits must be capped (suggest cap = 12% of committed contract value) and tied to a published index with a 14-day sustained movement trigger. Also, any credit greater than $75k requires VP of Finance approval and accounting must treat it as a contra-revenue item.

Action items for approval path:
- Hannah to finalize proposed cap and tranche points.
- Neha to draft the index-trigger clause and confirm accounting language.
- Marcus to prepare a condensed finance memo for VP approval if the recommended credit might exceed $75k.

I can draft the finance memo today if you confirm final numbers.

—Marcus

Quick operational confirmation from Dedicated product/SE perspective: the runtime can honor tiered pass-throughs and we have telemetry to detect index-driven cost spikes (we already consume market feeds for internal cost reporting). Implementation notes:

- If we add the index-trigger clause, engineering ops needs a clear mapping: which SKUs map to which index readings, and the expected invoice adjustment cadence (we recommend monthly adjustments with lookback).
- For the customer's July 7 board timeline, Hannah — please send the one-pager and the draft index clause. I'll prepare a short engineering note that explains how we'd monitor and the expected detection lag (usually 48–72 hours for signal confidence).

Requesting internal approval ask (Hannah): escalate to Sales Leader for a discretionary upfront credit authority of up to $75k to avoid requiring VP Finance signoff for smaller cases. If Marcus confirms $75k is the right threshold, we'll include that in the approval path to keep Helios' board timeline intact.

I'll also flag this with the Dedicated ops on-call so we can stand up a monitoring dashboard if Helios signs.
